adventure.title: Lanikai Pillbox Trail at Sunrise
adventure.description: A short, steep scramble up Kaiwa Ridge that puts you on a WWII bunker watching the sun come up behind the Mokulua Islands.
adventure.bonus: Nobody takes a photo until you've watched the sun fully clear the horizon.

adventure.title: Hike the Kuliʻouʻou Ridge Trail
adventure.description: Five miles and 1,800 feet through ironwood forest to a ridge-top bench with the whole windward coast laid out below you.
adventure.bonus: Sit on the summit bench for ten minutes before you start back down.

adventure.title: Snorkel with Turtles at Electric Beach
adventure.description: Warm outflow from the power plant across the road draws fish, turtles and sometimes spinner dolphins to this unglamorous but extraordinary West Side spot.
adventure.bonus: Swim out past the second buoy before you put your face in.

adventure.title: Skydive Over the North Shore
adventure.description: Fourteen thousand feet above Dillingham Airfield, with the whole reef line, the Waiʻanae range and the open Pacific under your feet.
adventure.bonus: Keep your eyes open the entire freefall.

adventure.title: Dive the Sea Tiger Wreck
adventure.description: A 189-foot freighter sunk on purpose off Waikīkī, now a reef structure patrolled by green sea turtles and whitetip sharks at 80 feet.
adventure.bonus: Hover motionless for a full minute and let the turtles come to you.

adventure.title: Kayak to the Mokulua Islands
adventure.description: Paddle forty minutes across turquoise water from Kailua Beach to land on a seabird sanctuary with a beach almost nobody reaches.
adventure.bonus: Swim to shore from the last fifty metres instead of paddling in.

adventure.title: Kaʻena Point to the Albatross Colony
adventure.description: A hot, exposed six-mile round trip along an old railbed to the westernmost tip of Oʻahu, where Laysan albatross nest metres from the trail.
adventure.bonus: Carry out one piece of someone else's litter.

adventure.title: Makapuʻu Point Lighthouse Trail
adventure.description: A paved coastal climb around the easternmost tip of Oʻahu, with tide pools below and, in winter, humpbacks breaching offshore.
adventure.bonus: Spot a whale before anyone else does.

adventure.title: Hike Diamond Head State Monument at Sunrise
adventure.description: Climb the switchback trail inside a volcanic crater to a WWII bunker lookout with a 360° view of Waikiki at first light.
adventure.bonus: Watch the sun clear the horizon from the summit before descending.

adventure.title: Climb the Koko Head Crater Stairs
adventure.description: Grind up over 1,000 aging railroad-tie steps up the side of a volcanic cone for one of Oahu's toughest views.
adventure.bonus: Don't stop for longer than 60 seconds at any point.

adventure.title: Zipline and ATV Tour at Kualoa Ranch
adventure.description: Zipline over the jungle valley made famous by Jurassic Park, then tear through it by ATV on a working cattle ranch.
adventure.bonus: Spot the film location you recognize from a movie.

adventure.title: Snorkel the Reef at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve
adventure.description: Snorkel a protected volcanic bay teeming with parrotfish, urchins, and the occasional honu sea turtle.
adventure.bonus: Spot five different fish species and name them.

adventure.title: Surf Lesson at Waikiki Beach
adventure.description: Catch your first (or fiftieth) wave with a local instructor on Waikiki's gentle, beginner-friendly breaks.
adventure.bonus: Stand up on a wave for at least three seconds.

adventure.title: Stand-up Paddleboard at Ala Moana Beach Park
adventure.description: Rent a paddleboard and glide across the calm, reef-protected lagoon right next to downtown Honolulu.
adventure.bonus: Try a full lap without kneeling down once.

adventure.title: Helicopter Tour Over Oahu's Coastline
adventure.description: Take a doors-on helicopter flight over Oahu's cliffs, waterfalls, and reefs that no road can reach.
adventure.bonus: Get a photo of a crater from directly above.

adventure.title: Hike Manoa Falls Through the Rainforest
adventure.description: Follow a muddy jungle trail under bamboo groves and banyan roots to a 150-foot waterfall.
adventure.bonus: Find the giant banyan roots and pose for a photo.

culture.title: Courtyards of the Honolulu Museum of Art
culture.description: Open-air courtyards link galleries holding one of the finest Asian art collections in the US, including a Japanese ukiyo-e holding of international rank.
culture.bonus: Sit in the Chinese courtyard until you've heard the fountain for a full minute.

culture.title: Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum on Ford Island
culture.description: Two original seaplane hangars still carrying bullet holes from 7 December 1941, now holding restored aircraft and a control tower you can climb.
culture.bonus: Find a bullet hole in the hangar glass before you leave.

culture.title: Torch Lighting and Hula at Kūhiō Beach
culture.description: At sunset the torches go up beside the Duke Kahanamoku statue and a hālau dances on the beachfront mound, free, and better than most paid lūʻau.
culture.bonus: Stay through the pau hana chant at the end.

culture.title: Hawaiian Hall at the Bishop Museum
culture.description: Three galleried floors of koa wood holding the world's great collection of Hawaiian and Pacific artefacts: feather capes, kapa, and a sperm whale over your head.
culture.bonus: Spend a full ten minutes with one object.

culture.title: Polynesian Cultural Center at Lāʻie
culture.description: Six island villages (Samoa, Aotearoa, Fiji, Tahiti, Tonga, Hawaiʻi) staffed by people from each, ending with the largest Polynesian night show in the world.
culture.bonus: Learn to do one thing in each village: climb, weave, drum, dance.

culture.title: ʻIolani Palace: America's Only Royal Palace
culture.description: The seat of the Hawaiian Kingdom, wired for electricity before the White House, and the room where Queen Liliʻuokalani was imprisoned after the overthrow.
culture.bonus: Read the queen's quilt panel all the way through.

culture.title: Shangri La, Doris Duke's Islamic Art House
culture.description: A heiress's oceanfront home at Black Point, filled over sixty years with Islamic tilework, textiles and a Mughal-inspired garden, small tours only.
culture.bonus: Pick the single room you'd move into.

culture.title: Lei Day at Kapiʻolani Park
culture.description: Every May Day the park fills with a lei-making contest, hula and the crowning of a Lei Queen, the most purely local celebration on the Honolulu calendar.
culture.bonus: Make your own lei and give it away before you leave.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Plate Lunch Roulette
8ball.description: Walk into the next plate lunch spot you pass, order the thing you've never heard of, and eat it on a sea wall.
8ball.bonus: Two scoops rice. No substitutions. No complaining.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Circle the Island
8ball.description: Drive the full loop of Oʻahu in one day (windward coast up, North Shore across, Waiʻanae side down) and stop at three beaches nobody picked in advance.
8ball.bonus: Swim at every single stop, no matter the weather.

chill.title: Golden Hour at the Nuʻuanu Pali Lookout
chill.description: Wind funnels straight up a thousand-foot cliff face here, and the whole windward coast opens out in front of you at once.
chill.bonus: Lean into the updraft and let it hold you.

chill.title: Beach Day at Lanikai
chill.description: Half a mile of powder sand and shallow, windless water on the windward side: no facilities, no lifeguards, no reason to leave.
chill.bonus: Stay in the water until your fingers wrinkle.

chill.title: Sundown at Sunset Beach
chill.description: Two miles of North Shore sand that in summer is a flat, warm swimming beach and in winter is the most famous wave-watching seat in the world.
chill.bonus: Stay until the last light is gone from the water.

chill.title: Exceptional Trees at Foster Botanical Garden
chill.description: Fourteen acres of 150-year-old canopy in the middle of downtown, including a cannonball tree and a bo tree grown from the original in Bodh Gaya.
chill.bonus: Find the biggest tree in the garden and stand at its base.

chill.title: Windward Coast Drive to Kualoa
chill.description: Take the Kamehameha Highway slowly up the windward side and stop at Kualoa Regional Park, where the Kōolau wall drops straight into the sea behind Chinaman's Hat.
chill.bonus: Stop at every fruit stand you pass.

chill.title: Tide Pools at Shark's Cove
chill.description: In summer the North Shore lava shelf goes glassy and fills with clear pools full of reef fish. An aquarium you can sit down in.
chill.bonus: Identify three fish without looking anything up.

chill.title: Reflect at Pearl Harbor's USS Arizona Memorial
chill.description: Take the boat out to the white memorial floating above the sunken USS Arizona and sit with the history of December 7th.
chill.bonus: Read at least three names on the memorial wall.

chill.title: Sunset at Waikiki Beach
chill.description: Claim a patch of sand on Waikiki Beach and watch the sky turn gold behind Diamond Head.
chill.bonus: Stay until the very last light disappears.

chill.title: Wander Lyon Arboretum's Rainforest Trails
chill.description: Walk quiet, shaded paths through 200 acres of tropical botanical collections at the back of Manoa Valley.
chill.bonus: Find three plants you can't name and look them up after.

chill.title: Visit Byodo-In Temple in the Valley of the Temples
chill.description: Ring the sacred bell and walk the koi ponds at this full-scale replica of a 900-year-old Japanese temple set against the Ko'olau cliffs.
chill.bonus: Ring the temple bell before you leave.

foodie.title: Musubi Run at Iyasume
foodie.description: Two dozen versions of spam musubi (egg, avocado, teriyaki, bacon) wrapped to order in Waikīkī and perfect for a beach morning.
foodie.bonus: Buy one musubi for a stranger on the beach.

foodie.title: Garlic Shrimp from Giovanni's Truck
foodie.description: The graffiti-covered truck in Haleʻiwa that started the North Shore shrimp truck phenomenon: twelve shrimp, two scoops of rice, an absurd amount of garlic.
foodie.bonus: Add your own line to the graffiti on the truck.

foodie.title: Açaí Bowl at Haleʻiwa Bowls
foodie.description: A walk-up window under the trees in Haleʻiwa serving the açai bowl the whole North Shore measures the others against.
foodie.bonus: Eat it sitting on the grass, not in the car.

foodie.title: Prawns at Romy's in Kahuku
foodie.description: A roadside shack on its own aquaculture ponds at the island's northern tip, serving prawns that were in the water an hour ago.
foodie.bonus: Order the prawns shell-on and eat them with your hands.

foodie.title: Oxtail Soup at Asahi Grill
foodie.description: Honolulu's benchmark bowl, clear ginger broth, fall-apart oxtail and a dish of grated ginger and shoyu on the side that you are supposed to use generously.
foodie.bonus: Finish the broth. All of it.

foodie.title: BYOB Sushi at Mitch's Fish Market
foodie.description: A dozen seats behind a wholesale fish counter near the airport, serving some of the freshest sashimi on the island. Bring your own bottle.
foodie.bonus: Let the chef decide the entire order.

foodie.title: Chef's Counter at Senia
foodie.description: Eight seats facing the pass in Chinatown for a tasting menu that reads like the most ambitious cooking in the state.
foodie.bonus: Ask the chef what they'd cook if nobody was watching.

foodie.title: Dinner at MW Restaurant
foodie.description: Wade Ueoka and Michelle Karr-Ueoka turn local plate-lunch memory into fine dining, the mochi-crusted ʻopakapaka and the candy bar dessert are the reasons to go.
foodie.bonus: Order the dessert first and make it work.

foodie.title: Home-Style Plate Lunch at Helenas Hawaiian Food
foodie.description: Order a James Beard Award-winning plate of pipikaula short ribs and lomi salmon at this family-run Kalihi institution.
foodie.bonus: Ask your server which dish the family recommends today.

foodie.title: Malasadas Fresh from Leonards Bakery
foodie.description: Order a box of hot, sugar-dusted Portuguese malasadas from the bakery locals have lined up for since 1952.
foodie.bonus: Try a filled flavor you've never had, custard or haupia.

foodie.title: Shave Ice at Waiola Shave Ice
foodie.description: Cool off with a mountain of finely shaved ice and tropical syrups at this Kapahulu neighborhood favorite.
foodie.bonus: Order a flavor combo you've never tried before.

foodie.title: Poke Bowl at Ono Seafood
foodie.description: Build a plate-lunch-style poke bowl at this no-frills counter locals swear is the best on the island.
foodie.bonus: Ask the counter which poke is selling out fastest today.

social.title: Beers at Honolulu Beerworks
social.description: A reclaimed-wood warehouse in Kakaʻako with a back patio, long communal tables and the best local beer list on the island.
social.bonus: Order the beer with the strangest name on the board.

social.title: Cocktails at Bar Leather Apron
social.description: Twenty-eight seats hidden inside a downtown office building, pouring what is routinely called the best cocktail program in the Pacific.
social.bonus: Order something off-menu and describe only a mood.

social.title: Late Night at Bar 35
social.description: Two hundred bottled beers and a back courtyard in Chinatown that's been the centre of Honolulu's late-night scene for two decades.
social.bonus: Pick a beer from a country nobody at the table has been to.

social.title: Sunset Sail Off Waikīkī
social.description: Push off straight from the sand on a catamaran, get out past the reef and watch Diamond Head turn gold with a drink in your hand.
social.bonus: Sit on the trampoline at the bow the entire way out.

social.title: Tiki Night at La Mariana Sailing Club
social.description: The last authentic tiki bar in Honolulu, hung with salvaged fixtures from every tiki bar that closed before it, on a working boat harbour.
social.bonus: Sit at the piano bar and request something.

social.title: Mai Tais at House Without a Key
social.description: Under a century-old kiawe tree at the Halekulani, with live Hawaiian music, a former Miss Hawaii dancing hula and Diamond Head going pink behind her.
social.bonus: Stay for the whole hula set without checking your phone.

social.title: Friday Fireworks at Hilton Hawaiian Village
social.description: Every Friday night the lagoon end of Waikīkī gets a full fireworks show. Watch it free from the sand at Duke Kahanamoku Beach.
social.bonus: Get in the water and watch it from there.

social.title: Live Hawaiian Music at Kani Ka Pila Grille
social.description: The Outrigger Reef's courtyard hosts the best working Hawaiian musicians in Waikīkī nightly, slack key, falsetto and no cover charge.
social.bonus: Learn the name of one song you hear and look it up after.

social.title: Saturday Morning at KCC Farmers Market
social.description: Weave through 90+ local vendor stalls of tropical fruit, poke, and food trucks at the Kapiolani Community College Farmers Market.
social.bonus: Try a fruit you've never eaten before.

social.title: First Friday Art Walk Through Chinatown Honolulu
social.description: Bar-hop between pop-up galleries, live music, and street food stalls on Honolulu's monthly gallery night.
social.bonus: Talk to one artist about the piece you like most.

social.title: Sunset Happy Hour at Dukes Waikiki
social.description: Grab a table on the sand at this beachfront icon for mai tais and live Hawaiian music as the sun drops.
social.bonus: Request a song from the live band.
